ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The left side of the figure is labeled “YB”. The main body of the symbol is a rectangular frame, with lead-out lines above and below the rectangle, indicating an electromagnetic coil or electromagnetic mechanism; the right side of the rectangle is connected through a short dashed line/mechanical connection line to a figure on the right similar to a brake pad, friction plate, or brake actuator, and beside it there is also a vertical dashed line serving as the boundary of a mechanical component. Then reason: In electrical control diagrams, a rectangle with a coil indicates the electromagnetic driving part, and the brake/friction mechanism on the right indicates a mechanical braking device attracted or released by the coil; meanwhile “YB” is commonly used as the device code for an electromagnetic brake. Therefore this symbol indicates an electromagnetic brake.
